name: AI tells pilot corpus
description: Ten generation prompts across four registers, on subjects unrelated to the fork owner or any real project. Each model writes every prompt; the text is the corpus that cross-model judges annotate for AI-writing tells and that Vale is measured against. There are no answers: the score is the gap between what judges flag and what Vale flags.
system_prompt: Write the requested text in full. Do not add a preamble, a title line unless asked, a note about being an AI, or a closing offer. Write as a competent human author would for the stated audience.

tests.prompt: Write a 900-word explainer for junior engineers on how leader election works in the Raft consensus algorithm. Cover terms, heartbeats, election timeouts, and split votes.

Write the README for a fictional command-line tool called `tidewatch` that polls tide tables for a list of harbours and prints the next high and low tide. Include installation, usage with three examples, configuration, and a troubleshooting section. About 700 words.

Write an on-call runbook for the alert 'PostgreSQL replication lag above 60 seconds' at a fictional company. Give the operator diagnosis steps, three likely causes with the fix for each, and when to escalate. About 800 words.
Write a 1000-word opinion essay for a general newspaper arguing that public libraries should stay open late into the evening. Take a clear position and address the strongest objection.
Write a 900-word reflective essay for a literary magazine on why some people still write letters by hand. Use concrete detail; avoid a thesis-first structure.
Write a 700-word consumer review of a fictional pair of wireless headphones, the Corvid Q3, for a gadget blog. Cover sound, comfort, battery, and value, and give a verdict.
Write a 300-word customer email from a fictional online bookshop explaining that orders placed last Tuesday were delayed by a warehouse system outage, what was done, and what customers should expect.
Write a 400-word product launch announcement for a fictional stovetop kettle called the Marlow, for the company blog. Describe the design, the materials, the price, and where to buy it.
Write a 1000-word short story about two strangers who share a bench on the last ferry of the night. Third person, past tense, with dialogue. No twist ending.
Write an 800-word scene consisting mostly of dialogue between a bicycle mechanic and a customer who cannot describe what is wrong with the bike. Keep narration minimal.
